newsitem.title: USA: Mississippi House approves tax cut for couples.
newsitem.headline: Mississippi House approves tax cut for couples.

text.p: The Mississippi House of Representatives has approved a proposal to phase out the "marriage penalty" in the state's income tax, a legislative clerk said.
The House bill approved 118-3 on Thursday would make the tax rate for married couples equal to that for two unmarried people.
Gov. Kirk Fordice has promised to sign the bill as soon as it reaches his desk. But legislators must first work out differences between the House bill and one previously approved in the Senate.
Both would increase the standard deduction for married couples who do not itemize to $4,600 from $3,400 and raise the personal exemption to $12,000 from $9,500.
For single filers, the deduction would remain $2,300 and the exemption $6,000.
The House version would phase in the changes over four years.
The Senate version would increase the deduction in the first year and raise the exemption over three years.
Once fully implemented, the propsoal would reduce married couples' tax bill by $185 to $200 a year.
